title: The joint-stock company
summary: In a joint-stock company, people invested capital and received part of the profits. A royal charter created the English East India Company as one on 31 December 1600. The Dutch East India Company followed in 1602; members of the public could buy its shares, and it is considered the first publicly traded company. Britain's Registration Act of 1844 and Limited Liability Act of 1855 then opened such companies more widely, and 2,488 limited liability companies formed between 1856 and 1862.
